name: Aceh-Tohoku Seismic Forecasting Benchmark
description: Seismic magnitude forecasting in megathrust zones poses a critical challenge for disaster mitigation, necessitating a rigorous balance between prediction accuracy and computational latency. This study presents a comparative evaluation between a Transformer-based Deep Learning model (Informer) and an adaptive statistical method (Rolling ARIMA) for earthquake magnitude prediction. Case studies were conducted in two seismically active regions: Aceh (Sunda Megathrust) and Tohoku (Japan Trench), using USGS catalog data spanning 1990-2024. Experiments were performed across multiple temporal scales (daily, weekly, monthly) and prediction horizons. Results indicate that while the Informer excels in minimizing relative error (SMAPE) on large-volume datasets, Rolling ARIMA demonstrates significant superiority in shortterm accuracy ($\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ up to 0.92 in Aceh) and stability under limited data scenarios. reputation: A domain-specific forecasting benchmark for seismic magnitude prediction, mainly of interest to earth-science and forecasting researchers rather than a broad ML community standard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results depend on region, temporal scale, and prediction horizon, and the paper emphasizes a tradeoff between accuracy and latency.
